title: Automated machine learning predicts screening-level PTSD in Danish soldiers
summary: Automated machine learning applied to routine data from three cohorts of Danish soldiers (N = 232 to 352) predicted screening-level PTSD 2.5 and 6.5 years after deployment, with random forest AUC 0.77 and 0.78. Models transferred between cohorts; military rank, hyperarousal and total PTSD symptoms were the most predictive. Linear models performed equally well, outcomes are self-reported screening measures and cohorts are small.
ai_technology: Automated machine learning model selection (random forest best; linear models equal)
organization: Danish Veterans Centre; University of Copenhagen

evidence.tested: Transfer of models across three independent deployment cohorts (N = 232 to 352).
evidence.unknown: Clinical use for targeting interventions; diagnostic-level PTSD outcomes; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Automated model and parameter selection built models predicting later screening-level PTSD.
